study type: Interrupted time series analysis using the Georgian Birth Registry
exposure: Introduction of a financial penalty for hospitals not meeting cesarean section reduction targets
outcome: Neonatal intensive care unit transfer rate
cohort: 150,534 women who gave birth in Georgia from 2017 to 2019, representing nearly all births in the country during this time.
finding: The cesarean section rate in Georgia decreased from 44.7% to 40.8% after the introduction of a financial penalty for hospitals not meeting cesarean section reduction targets, with the largest decrease observed among primiparous women, those <25 years of age, and those with higher education.
